messages.subject: bruvo.dist by pops?
parts:
Hi,

Wanted to inquire how to make poppr compute a tree (bootstrapped) from SSR matrix [65Ind x 28SSR], but at the population level. Similar to this: 

MyGenindObject %>%
  genind2genpop() %>%
  aboot(cutoff = 50, quiet = TRUE, sample = 1000, distance = nei.dist, ploidy = 2)

bruvo.boot (alone) gives me a nj/upgma tree on individual level, which is too busy. bruvo.boot in the code above screams error 
"Error in genind2df(gen, sep = "/", usepop = FALSE) : 
  x is not a valid genind object", though imported my data as read.genalex(., geneclone = FALSE) and class() = genind.

Any help in the right direction is much appreciated!
-m

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] bruvo.dist by pops?
parts:
Hello,

The error you are getting is due to the fact that genind2genpop() converts your genind object to a genpop object. 

There is currently no *automated* way of performing this operation since Bruvo's distance was only designed for individuals.  Moreover, to complicate matters, the data is internally transformed to a different format (called "bruvomat"). Basically, you're going to have to roll your own. 

My recommendation would be to use the boot.phylo() function in ape with a "bootgen" object (use new("bootgen", mydata) for that [1]) and a custom function that will:

1. convert your bootgen object to a genind object
2. feed it into Bruvo's distance
3. calculate the average distance between populations
4. create a tree from this distance

A couple of things you should consider:

A. You will need to make sure your data is coded in repeat lengths, not fragment lengths. One way bootgen objects work is by not particularly caring what the names of the loci are, but this has the side effect of being useless for Bruvo's distance on observed fragment lengths. 
B. I do not know how one would deal with within-population variance when calculating population-level distances from an individual distance.

At some point in the future, I will add a way to calculate Bruvo's distance directly on a matrix/data frame but that day hasn't come yet. 

Hope that helps,
Zhian


[1]: https://grunwaldlab.github.io/poppr/reference/coercion-methods.html
